note.p: Booth was an actor of some renown who first gained public notice in supporting roles to Edmund Kean before appearing in competition with Kean. He emigrated to America in 1812 where he lived for the rest of his life. He returned to England in 1825 and 1836 for brief visits. He was the father of Edwin Thomas Booth, renowned American tragedian, and John Wilkes Booth, Abraham Lincoln's assassin.

It seems likely that he re-connects with Godwin, perhaps especially in the earlier trip in 1825, but Godwin is not clearly distinguishing him from David Booth. We have attributed appearances to Booth in the company of people from the world of theatre which we think begins in the August of 1824 and concludes in that of 1825.

person.bibl: Stephen M. Archer, Junius Brutus Booth, Theatrical Prometheus (Carbondale, Il.: Southern Illinois University Press, 1992)
